senses.definition: A post bearing a sign that gives information on directions.
senses.example: Dozens of signposts have been stolen, forcing the local authorities to put up the sign at a 2m height and embed it in theft-resistant concrete when putting up replacements.

senses.definition: A word or phrase within a clue that serves as an indicator, rather than being fodder.
senses.example: In the first example — Dance revolutionised Burma — you know the middle word is the signpost as revolutionised is too long to be the fodder (or letters to scramble). […] And bang, out jumps RUMBA.
The route wasn't signposted, and we got lost on the way.

senses.definition: To direct (somebody) to services, resources, etc.
senses.example: We believe that some Carers' Centres already offer an effective 'first stop shop' for signposting carers to local organisations, services and benefits, and for providing ongoing support as carers' circumstances change.

senses.definition: To signal (something) intentionally, as if with a signpost.
